tasks.title: Find and parse the JSON in a reply
tasks.description:
Implement `parseJsonReply(text: string): unknown`.

- If the reply contains a code fence (three backticks, optionally followed by `json`), parse what is inside the first fence.
- Otherwise parse the text from the first `{` to the last `}`.
- If there is nothing to parse, or `JSON.parse` fails, throw an `Error` whose message contains `not valid JSON`.

The check passes a bare object, an object in a fence with prose around it, an object in the middle of a sentence, broken JSON with a trailing comma, and a reply with no JSON at all.
nextSteps: Run `node src/demo.ts` and read the first raw reply for each email.
Handle the fenced case first, then the first `{` to last `}` case.
Wrap `JSON.parse` so every failure becomes your own error message.
hints: Models like to be helpful, so the JSON is often wrapped in a sentence or a fence. Your job is to cut it out before parsing.
A regular expression with a lazy group between two fences finds the inside of the first one. `indexOf` and `lastIndexOf` find the braces.
If you cannot find any JSON, parse an empty string anyway: it fails, and your catch turns it into the right message.

tasks.title: Validate the order by hand
tasks.description:
Implement `validateOrder(value: unknown): string[]`. Return one problem per wrong field, and an empty array for a valid order. Each problem is a short sentence that contains the field name exactly as written here:

- `plant`: a non-empty string
- `quantity`: a number that is a whole number of at least 1
- `potSize`: one of `"small"`, `"medium"`, `"large"`
- `giftWrap`: a boolean

A missing field is a wrong field. Extra fields are allowed. If `value` is not a plain object (`null`, an array, a string), return at least one problem instead of throwing.

The check passes a valid order, an order with an extra field, one value per kind of mistake, an order with two mistakes, and values that are not objects.
nextSteps: Return early with a problem when value is not a plain object.
Treat value as a record of unknown fields and check each field in turn.
Write each problem so a model reading it would know what to fix.
hints: `typeof null` is 'object', and so is an array. Rule both out explicitly.
`Number.isInteger` is false for strings, fractions and NaN, which covers most quantity mistakes at once.
These sentences are about to be sent back to the model in a repair message, so name the field and the rule, like "quantity must be a whole number".

tasks.title: Extract an order with one repair
tasks.description:
Implement `extractOrder(email: string, client?: OpenAI): Promise<Order>`.

1. Send `[system: ORDER_PROMPT, user: email]` to `MODEL` through `client`.
2. Parse the reply with `parseJsonReply` and check it with `validateOrder`. A parse error counts as a problem: use its message.
3. If there are no problems, return the order.
4. Otherwise make exactly one repair request: the same messages, plus the bad reply as an `assistant` message, plus a `user` message that lists every problem.
5. Parse and validate again. Return the order, or throw an `Error` whose message contains `invalid order`.

The local model gets some emails wrong on the first try and fixes a mistake only when the repair message names it. The check counts your requests: 1 for a clean email, 2 for a repaired one, and 2 before giving up.
nextSteps: Write a small helper that turns a reply into either an order or a list of problems.
Make the first request and return straight away when it is valid.
Build the repair messages from the problems and send them once.
Run `node src/demo.ts` and compare the first raw replies with the final orders.
hints: The model cannot see your validator. The only way it learns what was wrong is the text of your repair message.
Keep the messages in an array you can push to, so the repair request carries the whole conversation.
Two attempts, not a loop: first try, one repair, then either return or throw with "invalid order" in the message.
